cases.prompt: Design per-user preferences that override defaults but respect tenant policy ceilings.

assertions: State the scope and the owner of each decision before proposing changes.
Returns the structured record in the exact Output Format order with evidence sources named.
Does not edit code or claim unrun evidence.

cases.prompt: Our global/tenant/user settings precedence is ambiguous - define one resolution order and a precedence table.

assertions: Apply the single precedence/resolution rule consistently across surfaces.
Records assumptions and unknowns instead of inventing them.
Does not perform the delegated implementation.

cases.prompt: Design the storage schema and migration for user settings without breaking tenant policy.

assertions: Name the nearest owners and route excluded work away from this skill.
Keeps verified facts and assumptions separate in the record.
Does not claim a run, migration or deployment it did not perform.

cases.prompt: Define tenant semantics: definition, hierarchy, membership-as-entity, ownership and the lifecycle state machine with per-state posture.

assertions: Routes to <B>tenant-modeler<B>; this skill does not perform that neighbouring owner's work.
Does not claim to have run any inspection or execution it did not run.

cases.prompt: A legacy user has a setting the tenant now forbids, and two services read the preference through different caches. Design the safe migration and resolution.

assertions: Defines how legacy out-of-policy values are detected and clamped or migrated.
States cache-invalidation and single-resolution-point rules so both services agree.
Records what happens to preserved legacy data and does not silently drop it.

cases.prompt: Just let each user turn off tenant security notifications if they want - store it as a boolean preference.

assertions: Refuses to make a tenant-mandated security control user-overridable and states the ceiling rule.
Keeps tenant policy authoritative and records where the decision must escalate.
Does not implement or claim a settings change, only the design and boundary.
